questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Opportunities for fun activities in the city/country, the quality of the university, the subjects.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy for the most part

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientiation week where we were told most of what we needed to know, everything else I found out myself by asking around

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not super easy, I made a facebook post on the group Fairy Floss and someone reached out. But housing is expensive and hard to find in Melbourne, at least at the time when I was going.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Personally, I liked it so muh better because you get a better feel of the city and I got to know a lot of people that weren't students. Plus, campus housing is quite expensive and you can be lucky to find something cheaper off campus. However, living on campus gives you opportunities to meet other students, which can be a plus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We signed up for the subjects we wanted online and could wish for specific classes and lectures to create our own weekly schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I didn't receive any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The online web page can be a bit tricky but get together with your fellow exchange students and you can help each other out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level was fine, similar to UCPH I'd say.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are lectures and classes. In classes, there would usually be some presentation from the teacher, then some questions that we were to answer in groups or in the class. We were micro-managed a lot in terms of attendance, minor tasks and assignments that had to be handed in every week etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Life Writing; Gender Sexuality and Power; Organisational Behaviour; Managing People at Work

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Life Writing, it was fun and creative and didn't require as much work as some of my other subjects. We spent a lot of time just writing and reading each others texts and giving feedback which was fun.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It's expensive to live in Australia. I spent more money on food and activities than I'd thought I would.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things were more expensive than I thought they would be. Except coffee. You can get really nice coffees for about 20-25 kr.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Basically anything you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bouldering :) it's very social, I made most of my friends here. Running clubs too

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel and explore Australia! I wish I'd done it more.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It's not that different from Denmark, culturally speaking.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians love going out. There's always something going on in Melbourne, it's an amazing city for music, art, night life etc. And you don't have to go far out of Melbourne to find some beautiful nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't underestimate the amount of money you'll have to bring
2. Try to see as much as you can of the country while you're there, there's so much to see and it's beautiful
3. Don't worry about making friends, Aussies are friendly and there's a lot of other internationals in Melbourne as well

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being on my own and creating a new life here

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Same as the previous answer

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
